slot.brief: Two projectiles fired with complementary angles with same speed; compare their ranges, maximum heights and times of flight qualitatively.

stem: Two balls are projected from the same point on horizontal ground with the same speed at angles of $35^\circ$ and $55^\circ$ with the horizontal. If their horizontal ranges are $R_1$ and $R_2$, maximum heights are $H_1$ and $H_2$, and times of flight are $T_1$ and $T_2$ respectively, then:

verdicts.working: Angles 35° and 55° are complementary (sum 90°), so R = u²sin2θ/g gives R1 = R2. H = u²sin²θ/(2g) and T = 2u sinθ/g both increase with θ in (0°,90°), so H1 < H2 and T1 < T2. Numeric check: R = 9.589 both; H = 1.68 vs 3.42; T = 1.17 vs 1.67.

working:
The angles of projection are $\theta_1 = 35^\circ$ and $\theta_2 = 55^\circ$. Since $\theta_1 + \theta_2 = 90^\circ$, these are complementary angles.

1. Horizontal Range:
$$R = \dfrac{u^2 \sin(2\theta)}{g}$$
For $\theta_1 = 35^\circ$, $\sin(2\theta_1) = \sin 70^\circ$.
For $\theta_2 = 55^\circ$, $\sin(2\theta_2) = \sin 110^\circ = \sin(180^\circ - 70^\circ) = \sin 70^\circ$.
Hence, $R_1 = R_2$.

2. Maximum Height:
$$H = \dfrac{u^2 \sin^2\theta}{2g}$$
Since $35^\circ < 55^\circ$, $\sin 35^\circ < \sin 55^\circ \implies \sin^2 35^\circ < \sin^2 55^\circ$.
Hence, $H_1 < H_2$.

3. Time of Flight:
$$T = \dfrac{2u \sin\theta}{g}$$
Since $\sin 35^\circ < \sin 55^\circ$, we have $T_1 < T_2$.

Thus, $R_1 = R_2$, $H_1 < H_2$, and $T_1 < T_2$.

Independent check: Angles 35° and 55° are complementary (sum 90°), so R = u²sin2θ/g gives R1 = R2. H = u²sin²θ/(2g) and T = 2u sinθ/g both increase with θ in (0°,90°), so H1 < H2 and T1 < T2. Numeric check: R = 9.589 both; H = 1.68 vs 3.42; T = 1.17 vs 1.67.

draft.distractor_notes:
Option A assumes that the projectile with a longer time of flight must also travel a greater horizontal distance, forgetting the complementary angle property for ranges.
Option C confuses the angle with the vertical or reverses the sine dependence, incorrectly predicting greater height and flight time for the smaller angle.
Option D incorrectly inverts the time-of-flight dependence (e.g., confusing $\sin\theta$ with $\cos\theta$ or horizontal velocity).
